topline.text: Today is payment day for the 2026 Schools Budget Support Grant - about £635m nationally going out to local authorities - but it's a continuation of existing cost-pressure funding, not new Budget money.
DfE still hasn't published its own breakdown of Wednesday's Budget settlement, so keep treating school-funding figures doing the rounds - including on the SEND gap - as provisional.
Today is the final day of Sheffield schools' autumn half term; pupils return Monday 2 November - check individual academy calendars rather than assuming a uniform city-wide date.
Reminder: the NEU's formal strike ballot over pay, funding and workload is still open and closes 15 December.

diary.text: Sheffield schools' autumn half term - today is the final day.
First Schools Budget Support Grant 2026 payments go out to local authorities.
Sheffield schools return from half term.
NEU's formal strike ballot over pay, funding and workload closes.
UK City of Culture 2029 winner announced; Sheffield is one of four finalists.

items.body: DfE is distributing roughly £635m nationally this financial year through the Schools Budget Support Grant 2026, covering centrally employed local-authority staff plus early years and post-16 provision; the first tranche reaches local authorities today, with academies paid in November. It's a continuation of existing cost-pressure support rather than new Budget money - the mainstream-schools element has already been folded into the national funding formula for 2026-27.
items.action: Check your local authority's payment schedule if you're relying on this grant for centrally-employed-staff costs this term.

items.body: Two days on from Chancellor John Healey's Budget, DfE has yet to publish its own schools-funding breakdown of the settlement. Keep holding off on budget-planning assumptions, including on the scale of the SEND funding gap, until that lands.

Today is the final day of Sheffield's autumn half term before pupils return on Monday 2 November. Academies can set their own calendar, so it's worth checking individual school dates rather than assuming a uniform city-wide return.
